The system MUST implement an RBAC permissions matrix with predefined roles: Admin, Supervisor, Reliability Engineer, Advanced Planner, Technician, Contractor. Each operation defines permitted roles.
The system MUST record all denied access attempts in the audit trail [TR-001] to detect privilege escalation attempts.
The system MUST support ownership-based access control: resources created by a user are accessible only by them, their supervisor, or an administrator.
Tokens must expire at the end of the working day (8 hours). The client must support automatic renewal or re-authentication.
Token signing keys must be securely stored in environment variables or a secrets manager.
Authorization verification MUST NOT add more than 5ms of latency to the request.
The system must mitigate security compromises via short token expiration and/or validation of the user's active state in the database.
The system MUST maintain a local replica of operational data necessary to operate offline: Work Orders, Equipment Units, schedules, and document metadata.
The system MUST enqueue operations performed offline with synchronization metadata (operation type, entity, data, synchronization state).
The system MUST automatically synchronize upon detecting connectivity, processing the queue in chronological order.
The system MUST implement incremental synchronization: transferring only records modified since the last successful synchronization.

The system MUST resolve synchronization conflicts by preserving all operational transactions executed offline, processing them in strict chronological order against core business rules. Upon discrepancies, the system MUST register the event and issue an alert for administrative reconciliation, preventing silent loss of historical records.
The system MUST implement retries with exponential backoff for failed synchronizations, notifying the user after exhausting attempts.
The local database must be encrypted [TR-002] using a key derived from the user's credentials. Without credentials, local data must be inaccessible.
Normative Reference: OWASP Mobile Security Top 10 (Insecure Data Storage)

Description: The local cache must have a configurable size limit to avoid exhausting device storage, eliminating old records without pending operations.
The interface must clearly display the synchronization state (synchronized, pending, failed) with a timestamp of the last successful synchronization.
Normative Reference: Nielsen Norman Group (NN/g) - Visibility of System Status

Description: Successful synchronizations must be recorded in the server's audit trail [TR-001].

The system MUST implement the master taxonomic hierarchy conforming to ISO 14224:2016, using standardized nomenclature for its levels and avoiding synonyms or local tags that alter the data model semantics.
The system MUST validate component uniqueness: a Maintainable Item (Level 8) CANNOT belong to two Equipment Units (Level 6) simultaneously.
The system MUST validate hierarchical integrity: each Equipment Unit must have a valid parent and a complete path from Level 1 must exist. Prevent deletion of parent levels with assigned dependents.
The system MUST expose services to query Equipment Units by hierarchical level and full path from Level 1.
The system MUST prevent cycles in the hierarchy: an Equipment Unit cannot be the parent of its own ancestor, directly or indirectly.
The system MUST support searching and filtering Equipment Units by level, criticality, and operational status, and generate taxonomic coverage reports.
Uniqueness validations and searches by level must execute in <500ms for catalogs of up to 50,000 Equipment Units.
Hierarchy creation/modification operations must be transactional: if validation fails, all changes are rolled back.
Validation errors must be specific and actionable, indicating exactly which component and relationship caused the problem.
Hierarchy violations and taxonomy changes must be recorded in the audit trail [TR-001].
The system MUST abstract integration with multiple AI providers behind a unified interface, supporting provider switching without affecting business logic and automatic failover.
The system MUST implement a confidence score (0-100) for all AI operations, with visual indicators: green (>=85%), yellow (70-84%), red (<70%). Red results require manual validation.
Normative Reference: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (RMF) - Explainability

Description: The system MUST record in the audit trail [TR-001] all AI invocations including: model, prompt hash, result hash, confidence score, user identifier.
The system MUST support fallback to manual processing: if the AI service is unavailable or confidence is insufficient, the user can complete fields manually.
AI service invocation must complete in <30 seconds (95th percentile). If it exceeds 45 seconds, return an error and suggest manual fallback.
AI budget control shall be delegated to the provider's console via Hard Limits, not requiring an internal billing dashboard for the MVP.
Data sent to external AI services MUST NOT contain Personally Identifiable Information (PII) unnecessary for the operation.
The system MUST maintain persistent connections with connected clients, featuring automatic disconnection detection.
The system MUST publish critical changes to all connected clients with <1 second latency: Work Permit (LOTO) changes, inventory movements, Work Order status updates.
The system MUST synchronize user permissions in <10 seconds: if an administrator revokes a permission, the change must reflect in the affected user's active session.
The system MUST implement authorization control on notifications: only sending updates to clients with authorized roles to view that information.
The system must support 1000+ simultaneous connections without performance degradation.
The interface must render updates without flickering. Objective: >=30 FPS on mobile, >=60 FPS on desktop.
If the real-time channel (e.g., SSE) is unavailable, the system must gracefully degrade to periodic polling.
The system MUST employ a neutral gray palette for operational screen backgrounds, minimizing non-functional contrast to reduce visual fatigue.
The system MUST reserve the use of saturated colors (Red, Yellow, Orange) exclusively for signaling alarms or critical safety states.
Normative Reference: The High Performance HMI Handbook (Color Coding)

Description: The system MUST prefer analog-style indicators (moving bars, gauges with shaded normal ranges) over simple digital values to provide immediate context.
The system MUST avoid decorative animations (e.g., spinning pumps, moving flow) unless they represent a critical safety warning.
The alarm color palette must comply with the WCAG 2.1 AA standard to guarantee legibility for individuals with color blindness.
Normative Reference: W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 AA

Description: The contrast between the gray background and static elements (piping, vessels) must be sufficient for visibility under high-illumination plant conditions.
Normative Reference: The High Performance HMI Handbook (Contrast Ratios)

Description: The system shall allow the configuration of preventive plans associated with cumulative usage variables (e.g., hour meters, cycle counters, processed volume).
Related Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)

Description: The system shall provide an API interface (REST endpoint) to receive external counter readings originating from SCADA systems or IoT devices.
Related Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)

Description: The system shall calculate the cumulative usage value and automatically trigger the creation of a Work Order when telemetry reaches or exceeds the configured threshold.
Related Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)

Description: The system shall block the processing of usage readings presenting values lower than the historical cumulative of the Equipment Unit to prevent misadjustments due to incorrect resets.
Related Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)

Description: The Planner may manually record counter readings from the Equipment Unit's technical record as a fallback mechanism against telemetry failures.
Related Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)

Description: The processing of the telemetry frame and the evaluation of Work Order trigger rules must not exceed 3 seconds from ingestion.
Related Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)

Description: The IoT data reception channel must implement authentication and TLS 1.3 encryption to prevent the injection of malicious telemetry data.
Normative Reference: NIST SP 800-52 (TLS 1.3 Guidelines) / OWASP IoT Top 10
Related Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)

Description: The system shall maintain the precision of cumulative counters using high-precision data types to prevent rounding errors in massive operations.
Related Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)

Description: The system shall provide a technical interface to perform the substitution of a physical Level 6 Equipment Unit assigned to a Level 5 (or lower) Functional Location.
Upon executing the substitution, the system shall atomically update the uninstalled Equipment Unit's status to "In Repair", "Damaged", or "In Storage" according to user selection.

The system shall validate that the selected replacement Equipment Unit is in an "Available" or "In Stock" status within the warehouse, blocking the operation if it is already linked to another location or out of service.
Following substitution, the system shall associate the new physical Equipment Unit to the Functional Location, immediately changing its operational status to "Operational".

The system shall mandatorily record the rotation details in the audit log: Functional Location identifier, uninstalled Equipment Unit Tag, installed Equipment Unit Tag, user, timestamp, and the Work Order justifying the action.
The Equipment Unit substitution transaction must execute under a single-commit schema in the database to ensure unlinking and linking actions are applied together or fail entirely.
The update of the hierarchical structure and the status change of both Equipment Units must complete in < 2 seconds on the server.
The system shall render vectorial plans ensuring interactive compatibility (panning and selection) across mobile and desktop devices.
The system shall dynamically link the graphic elements of the plan with the physical Equipment Unit records in the master catalog, guaranteeing a bidirectional correspondence.
Upon selecting a mapped geometry, the system shall deploy a contextual information panel including: Identifier (Tag), Operational Status, Criticality, and physical variables.
The inspection panel shall present real-time updates of the sensors associated with the selected equipment, automatically reflecting telemetry changes.
The system shall apply the HPHMI philosophy [TR-011], utilizing neutral backgrounds and reserving high-contrast colors exclusively for alarms or anomalies.
Normative Reference: The High Performance HMI Handbook (Color Coding)

Description: The initial load of the vectorial plan and asset mapping must complete in < 2 seconds over standard industrial networks.
The update of telemetry readings in the side panel must reflect in < 1 second from data reception at the server [TR-010].
The rendering engine must maintain a minimum rate of 30 FPS during map panning and zooming on mobile devices.
